clue.text: Lads I'm organising are gloomy

indicators.note: organising means putting things into a new order, so the letters before it get rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone is grumbling that the boys they are in charge of are a miserable bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and gloomy are synonyms, both describing a depressing, cheerless mood or outlook.

clue.text: Turn away and cleverly evade it

indicators.note: cleverly suggests skilful rearrangement, so the following letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Advice to dodge a problem by swerving and slipping away skilfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to depart or turn aside from a set course, so to turn away.

clue.text: Saucy dance

definitions.note: an adjective cluing a noun: read as 'sauce-like thing', a spicy sauce
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a spicy Mexican tomato sauce
second meaning: a lively Latin American dance

explanation.walkthrough: Saucy seems to describe a cheeky, suggestive dance; taken literally it points to a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is both a spicy relish served with Mexican food and an energetic Latin dance style.

clue.text: Idiotic, like one over the eight

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
the Roman numeral for one
the number that comes above eight

explanation.surface: Someone acting foolishly, like a person who has had one drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is a British idiom for slightly drunk; here it splits into one and a number past eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means stupid, literally donkey-like, so it is a synonym of idiotic.

clue.text: Young animals' muscles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the young of cattle, elephants or whales
second meaning: the fleshy backs of the lower legs

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes the clue read as one phrase about animals' muscles; it is really two separate meanings of the same plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the plural both of the baby cow and of the muscular back part of the human leg.

clue.text: Era before New York welcomes in conservative business

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next in the order they are read

parts.note: an era is an age

indicators.note: to welcome someone in is to take them inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for New York
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A historical note about an earlier period before New York embraced conservative commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a company providing a service, such as a travel or advertising firm, so a business.

clue.text: Turned around AV service in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means in a muddle, so the letters before it are disordered

parts.note: the two words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A report that an audio-visual support team was in chaos and had to reverse things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned around' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the definition; the anagram signal is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is Latin for the other way round, meaning with the order reversed, as an adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Hot spot where star has elevated role

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: elevated means lifted up, and in a down clue a word read upwards runs backwards

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: A celebrity hangout where a famous performer has landed a prestigious part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' and 'role' suggest acting, but the star is the one in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered sunny place that catches and holds the warmth, so a hot spot.

clue.text: Drill city squad endlessly retrained to produce a sort of electronic display

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter of the word before it is dropped
retrained means taught again in a new way, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A city's squad goes through endless drills and retraining to put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The military-sounding surface hides an anagram of thirteen letters; drop the last letter of squad first.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid crystal displays, LCDs, are the flat screens used in watches, calculators and televisions.

clue.text: Shape of a cricket ground

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an egg-like rounded outline
second meaning: the famous Test venue in south London

explanation.surface: A question about what outline a cricket field has.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground in Kennington, which hosts Test matches; its name happens to describe the shape of many cricket fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Oval is an egg-like geometric outline, and also the name of a well-known stadium where cricket is played.

clue.text: Madly indiscreet and sparkling

indicators.note: doing something madly means doing it wildly and out of order, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a lively, glittering person who talks far too freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent surfaces shimmer with changing rainbow colours, so they look sparkling and lustrous.

clue.text: Alas, I'm turning into a sausage!

indicators.note: turning into something means changing form, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in horror, like a cartoon character, that they are being transformed into a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, highly seasoned Italian sausage usually eaten sliced and cold.

clue.text: Reveals United Nations shelters

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for the United Nations
shelters as a verb: protects or covers

explanation.surface: A news headline about the United Nations providing refuges, with a hint of an exposé.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover something is to take its covering away, so it reveals or exposes it.

clue.text: Ballots touch on conclusion initially agreed

parts.note: to touch on a subject is to mention or refer to it
a conclusion is an end

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: the opening letter of agreed

explanation.surface: A report that the votes touched on a conclusion that was agreed from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes on a single question, the Latin plural of referendum, so they are ballots.

clue.text: Adventure journalist made the most of

parts.note: an exploit is a daring deed or adventure
ED is short for editor, the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter on a daring trip got the most out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to use it to full advantage, so exploited means made full use of.

clue.text: Cane harvest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short riding whip
second meaning: the yield of a field

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sugar cane being gathered in; really cane is a whip, and harvest is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding crop is a short cane-like whip, and a crop is also the produce gathered from a field in a season.

clue.text: About to copy garment

parts.note: c. is short for circa, Latin for about
to ape someone is to copy or imitate them

explanation.surface: Someone is about to make a copy of a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; split it, and 'to' is just a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a sleeveless outer garment that hangs loosely from the shoulders.

clue.text: Chapter on problem shire exposes treasure

indicators.note: a problem word suggests trouble or disorder, so the letters after it are jumbled

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for chapter
the letters of the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A book chapter about trouble in a county reveals a hidden hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second. A shire is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to value it dearly, so treasure as a verb is a synonym of cherish.

clue.text: Completed course of study by degrees

definitions.meaning: first meaning: finished a degree course and received the qualification
second meaning: arranged in steps or marked with a scale

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one sentence, 'by degrees' seems to mean a student finished their studies with degrees; it is a separate meaning, gradual or stepped.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduated means having earned a university qualification, and also divided into gradual steps, like a measuring jug's marked scale.

clue.text: Disgrace ex-student diving into river

indicators.note: diving into something puts you inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a grad is a graduate, someone who has finished studying

explanation.surface: A former student shamed themselves by jumping into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river and a common crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to humiliate or lower them in esteem, so it is a synonym of disgrace as a verb.

clue.text: English quota made up right on the line

indicators.note: made up means invented or composed, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the letters of the word, rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An English allocation was arranged precisely along a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right on the line' reads as 'exactly on target'; 'the line' is the definition, a sailor's name for the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call the equator 'the Line', the imaginary circle dividing the northern and southern hemispheres.

clue.text: Enter church below jetty

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means placed underneath, so the first-named piece comes second

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: An instruction to go into a church that stands beneath a landing stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to penetrate or break into something, so it means to enter forcibly.

clue.text: Crimes changed one's life

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters that follow are put into a new order

parts.note: the two words taken letter by letter, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Committing crimes turned someone's whole life around.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonies are serious offences in law, so they are crimes in the plural.

clue.text: Mature woman in the band

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, so the single letter sits within the word for a band

parts.note: a band of musicians is a group
W is the standard abbreviation for woman

explanation.surface: A description of an older, mature woman playing in a pop band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' looks like an adjective describing the woman, but it is the verb to be defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow up is to mature, become adult and develop sensible ways; both are verbs.

clue.text: Should nothing come from thought?

parts.note: surface padding that doubles as a hint: an old word for nought, zero, spelt the same as the answer

indicators.note: something that comes from a word is found inside it, so the letters are lifted from within

parts.note: the last five letters of the word

explanation.surface: A philosophical question: can thinking ever produce nothing at all?
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing' adds a second hint: the answer is also an old word for nought, zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is a modal verb expressing duty or advisability, so it is a synonym of should.

clue.text: Winner Ian's answer about things from earlier times

parts.note: a victor is a winner
the name taken as written; the possessive joins it to what follows
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A winner called Ian giving his answer on a quiz about history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link here, joining the wordplay to what the answer is about; it does not signal any wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana are objects, styles and collectables from the Victorian era of the 19th century, so things from an earlier period.

clue.text: Pronounced way of walking to make an entrance

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken out, so we want a word that sounds the same as the phrase that follows

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking

explanation.surface: An exaggerated, theatrical way of walking used to make a grand entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' seems to mean marked or exaggerated, describing the walk; it signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is a hinged barrier that forms an entrance through a fence or wall.

clue.text: Minimised risks and sat on the fence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: protected against loss, as with a bet
second meaning: avoided committing to one side

explanation.surface: A cautious person who played safe and refused to take sides.
explanation.walkthrough: A hedge is also a kind of fence, which gives the second definition a neat echo.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge bets is to limit possible loss, and to hedge in an argument is to avoid giving a clear answer.

clue.text: Cretan mixed a delicious drink

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from Crete prepared a tasty cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the Greek gods, and the word now means any delicious beverage.
